title: Local rings of dimension zero are henselian
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a local ring of Krull dimension $0$, i.e. a local ring whose only prime ideal is $\mathfrak m$ (for example an Artinian local ring). Then $R$ is henselian in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]: for every finite $R$-algebra $B$ (a ring map $R\to B$ making $B$ a finitely generated $R$-module), every idempotent of $B/\mathfrak mB$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $B$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 06RS (lemma-local-dimension-zero-henselian, line 42571); its proof uses Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian) (10)=>(1), Lemma 05DR (lemma-finite-finite-fibres), Lemma 00GT (lemma-integral-no-inclusion), Lemma 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), Lemma 00JA (lemma-product-local). The strictly henselian variant (residue field separably closed) is lem-weil-pbc-dimension-zero-local-strictly-henselian, whose proof contains this argument.

proof.text: Convert ringKrullDim R = 0 to Ring.KrullDimLE 0 R using Ring.krullDimLE_iff. Mathlib Ring.KrullDimLE.nilradical_eq_maximalIdeal identifies the maximal ideal with the nilradical (KrullDimension/Zero.lean:151). Thus the maximal ideal is nil. This is a direct specialization of the dimension-zero local-ring API.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-of-nil-maximal-ideal] to the containment of the maximal ideal in the nilradical from step 1. This gives HenselianLocalRing R by finite Newton iteration without passing through the finite-algebra characterization.

For any commutative R-algebra B, show mB is contained in nilradical B: rewrite with Ideal.map_le_iff_le_comap, replace m by nilradical R, and apply IsNilpotent.map to each element. No finiteness assumption on B is needed for this containment.

The kernel of the surjective quotient map B to B/mB is mB, which is nil by step 3. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lift-idempotents-locally-nilpotent], realized by existsUnique_isIdempotentElem_eq_of_ker_isNilpotent, to obtain the unique idempotent lift. Combine this with step 2 to prove both clauses. The zero algebra and the stated independent universe are included.

split_report.summary: Split along Stacks 06RS (algebra.tex line 42571) and its proof. The DAG definition def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology takes idempotent lifting for finite algebras as the definition, so the 04GG (10)=>(1) passage of the source is written out directly: (1) the primes of a finite R-algebra B are finitely many, maximal, over m, with nil intersection (Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum, which carries 05DR, 00GT, 00E0); (2) B is the product of its localizations at them (Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-product-of-localizations-at-maximal, 00JA); (3) B/mB is the product of the nonzero local rings B_i/mB_i (elementary, written out); (4) idempotents of a product of local rings are 0/1 vectors, so reduction is a bijection (elementary, written out). The four steps are those of the reviewed node lem-weil-pbc-dimension-zero-local-strictly-henselian (steps 1-4), which contains this argument; no new node was needed. Statement unchanged; stmt_deps unchanged. Alternative noted: m is nil, hence mB is nil, and Mathlib's existsUnique_isIdempotentElem_eq_of_ker_isNilpotent (00J9, node lem-weil-pbc-lift-idempotents-locally-nilpotent) gives the lifting in two steps; the source route was kept.

reviewed.note: 4 steps following Stacks 06RS with 04GG (10)=>(1) written out: the primes of a finite R-algebra are finitely many and maximal with nil intersection (existing leaf); B = product of its localizations at maximal ideals (00JA leaf); reduction mod m factorwise; idempotents of a product of local rings lift uniquely. No new nodes. Stage 3: lem-weil-pbc-dimension-zero-local-strictly-henselian repeats these steps and could cite this node.
